findings.reason: the plan should name the mechanism it extends for the stop, the discharge and the declaration, or the author rebuilds what already exists.
findings.text: §1 proposes a dispatch-boundary stop, a discharge, and a new config declaration without citing any existing mechanism it searched; the same shape already lives in `_unmetered_dispatch_alternatives` and `_lane_declaration_finding` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3538` and `:3577`), the discharge registry `reckon/crew/refusals.py:19`, and the lane gate/hold (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:4248`, `reckon/crew/hold.py`)

findings.reason: naming the existing orchestrator-class owner forces a decision to extend it or a stated reason why a bare boolean must stand beside it.
findings.text: the declaration `serves_orchestrators` is proposed as a new per-backend key although flight already models the orchestrator capability class as a routing overlay (`roles.by_capability_class.orchestrator`, `reckon/schema/flight.yaml:738`); the plan does not say why that place cannot carry the fact

findings.reason: the section should extend the existing override/reason mechanism or say why it cannot, rather than add a fourth allow-flag with its own recording path.
findings.text: §2 adds `--allow-orchestrator-lane REASON` as a thin layer over the stop, beside the existing per-dispatch override family (`--allow-execution-mismatch`, `--allow-unreconciled-runs`, `--allow-unreviewed-plan` in `reckon/cli.py:1759`), and gives no reason the recording of a per-dispatch reason cannot reuse that override surface

findings.reason: one predicate-filtered candidate-lane helper should serve both callers so the enumeration cannot drift from the one the advisory already uses.
findings.text: the discharge is computed by `_orchestrator_lane_discharge_candidates`, which iterates `config["backends"]`, filters by a per-backend predicate, calls `resolve_role_override` and keeps `launch in ("cli","in-harness")` — a line-for-line duplicate of `_unmetered_dispatch_alternatives`; the owner of "name configured lanes that can resolve this node" is `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3538`

findings.reason: a discharge kept out of the registry is invisible to the census the plan quotes, so the section must register it there or say why the stop sits outside the refusal-registry owner.
findings.text: §1 arrives with a discharge while the discharge registry that the plan's own "42 refusal sites against 5 discharges" census is drawn from is `DISPATCH_REFUSAL_REMEDIES`; the plan composes its discharge text inside `_dispatch_orchestrator_lane_stop` instead of registering it with that owner

findings.reason: the sections must account for the interface surface they add, or state why nothing can be retired or merged.
findings.text: with cli_options 317 and refusal_families 23 supplied, §2 adds the CLI option `--allow-orchestrator-lane` and §1 as designed adds a refusal family, and neither section names a member it retires or merges (cli_options 317→318, refusal_families 23→24)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the fence is one predicate plus one stop composed in resolution, and it delegates lane resolution to `resolve_role_override` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:187`) rather than hiding behaviour behind a spread of parallel wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements candidate-lane enumeration instead of extending its owner, `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3538`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §2 adds the `--allow-orchestrator-lane` CLI option and §1 as designed adds a refusal family, and neither section names what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites only its sibling plan as prior art and names no codebase mechanism it searched, while `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3538` `_unmetered_dispatch_alternatives`, `reckon/crew/refusals.py:19` `DISPATCH_REFUSAL_REMEDIES`, `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:4248` `_dispatch_lane_gate`/`reckon/crew/hold.py`, and the flight `roles`→`by_capability_class.orchestrator` overlay (`reckon/schema/flight.yaml:738`) already exist beside what it adds.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the plan adds a stop-and-discharge layer beside the existing lane-advisory layer without saying why that layer cannot be extended.
